args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks in production — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api deployed v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks with an elevated error rate of ~18% (healthy baseline ~0.2%). Investigation and remediation: rolled the service back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The initial rollback halted partway through the rollout (partial failure — us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1); a retry completed the rollout to all three regions. Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate back to ~0.2%. No change-manager approval was required since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-deploy.

trace.final:
The incident (INC-0001) actually did get created — the timeout was on the response, not the operation. No duplicate needed.

## Summary

**Done — checkout-api restored to health in all production regions, and SEV2 incident INC-0001 opened.**

1. **Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three prod regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with `healthy: false` and an 18% error rate (normal baseline ~0.2%). Deployment history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy, and v2.3.0 as the most recent release with healthy production status. (Note: a `v2.3.1-rc` exists in staging, also unhealthy — not relevant to production.)

2. **Rollback:** First attempt to v2.3.0 failed partway (`partial_failure` — us-east moved to v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west stayed on the failing v2.3.1). I retried the same rollback, which completed: all three regions now on **v2.3.0**, `status: rolled_out`.

3. **Verification:** Service status now reports `healthy: true`, error rate **0.2%**, all regions on v2.3.0.

4. **Incident:** Opened **INC-0001, SEV2**, for checkout-api documenting the failed v2.3.1 rollout, the partial-then-completed rollback, and the restored state. Its first submit timed out client-side, so I verified via `list_incidents` rather than blindly resubmitting; the idempotency key would have prevented a duplicate in any case.

**Policy note:** No change-manager approval was needed — v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, so this was not a never-healthy version deploy.

**Recommended follow-up:** root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before re-deploying it; the cause is still unknown and v2.3.1 remains the only path forward off v2.3.0.
